text:
devon: FYI vendor sent updated lead times for H200 — 20-26 weeks if we place an order next week. need a call on reservation strategy for Q4 surge :alarm_clock:

zara: ugh that's long. do we have updated GPU-hour forecasts for Q4 to justify reservations? :thinking_face:

devon: short summary below. pulled from forecast pipeline this morning. main point: expected inference GPU-hours across regions (baseline -> Q4 peak): us-west 140k -> 210k (1.5x), eu-west 85k -> 145k (1.7x), ap-south 30k -> 45k (1.5x). overall ~1.55x seasonal bump.

anya: sounds right based on last year's holiday spike + new enterprise customers. question: which hardware mix will give best cost/latency? H200 vs H100 vs L40S tradeoffs?

simon: quick take: H200 has better FP16/Tensor performance for our large chat models, H100 is still solid for general purpose, L40S is ~cheaper for medium context embeddings and dense batching. reservation economics: if committed hours/month > ~12k, reservation pays off for H200.

zara: can we slot numbers? i'm going to run a simple calc, will post results.

zara: paste calc:
```
Assumptions:
- H200 reserved price (monthly equiv): $20/hour
- H200 on-demand: $34/hour
- L40S reserved: $9/hour
- L40S on-demand: $14/hour
Break-even H200 reserved vs on-demand ~= 12.4k hours/month
Break-even L40S ~= 11k hours/month
```

anya: thanks. if eu-west is hitting 145k hours peak that's ~4.8k hours/month per rack? we need to map to #cards. also network egress caps in eu-west mean we can't burst unlimited. that's a region constraint.

devon: yup — also cluster health note: last week's NIC flapping on two H100 boxes in us-west reduced effective capacity by ~8% for 6 hours. ops-bot alerted but we needed manual kube restart. need to factor a reliability buffer.

ops-bot: incident: us-west node gpu-uw-42 reported NIC flapping 2026-05-02T03:14Z -> resolved 2026-05-02T09:21Z (restarts applied) :rotating_light:

simon: propose conservative planning: add 12% reliability buffer and plan reservations to cover 85% of peak demand to allow autoscale headroom.

zara: with 1.55x seasonal and 12% buffer, total reserved-equivalent hours needed Q4 = round( (baseline_hours * 1.55) * 1.12 * 0.85 ). i'll run region split next.

zara: region split (rounded):
```
us-west reserved H200 hours: 140k * 1.55 * 1.12 * 0.85 ~= 207k hours (Q4 period)
eu-west reserved H200 hours: 85k * 1.55 * 1.12 * 0.85 ~= 126k hours
ap-south reserved L40S hours: 30k * 1.55 * 1.12 * 0.85 ~= 44k hours
```

anya: those are Q4 totals — divide by 3 months to get monthly reservation sizing. so us-west ~69k H200-hours/month which is well above break-even.

simon: ok that justifies reserving H200 capacity in us-west and eu-west. question: lead time risk — if vendor quote 20-26 weeks, ordering in June -> delivery late Oct/Nov. we need runway for setup, validation, and canary rollouts.

devon: ops + infra ask: prioritize H200 racks in regions where latency-sensitive chat customers are concentrated (us-west primary, eu-west second). L40S for embeddings/ap-south. also consider fallback H100 pool for non-critical workloads to absorb unmet demand during delivery window.

anya: check procurement: do we have CAPEX approval for X units? finance pinged me last week, they need a formal sizing + cost estimate to greenlight a committed spend.

zara: i'll assemble a one-pager with numbers and two options: (A) aggressive reservation (cover 95% peak), (B) conservative (cover 75% peak + on-demand fallback). want sign-off by 2026-06-10 to meet vendor window.

ops-bot: procurement reminder: lead-time windows updated for H200 suppliers. earliest ship window if PO sent by 2026-06-12 -> 20 weeks earliest.

devon: action items: 
- zara: one-pager (due 2026-05-15) with region split, monthly hours, cost deltas.
- simon: prepare CAPEX vs OPEX calc and risk note (due 2026-05-18).
- anya: confirm network egress limits in eu-west and whether we can bump quota before Q4 (owner: cloud-network).

zara: noted. i'll also include a short rollback/fallback plan (use H100 pools + routing policy to send non-latency-critical traffic to lower-cost L40S).

simon: also add a short note about reservation term — 1yr vs 3yr tradeoffs. 3yr gets lower hourly but more commitment risk; we may prefer 1yr for flexibility given model evolution.

devon: agreed. final ask: if we decide to reserve, let's commit to a staged procurement: 50% in first PO (cover critical regions), 50% after validation. reduces delivery risk and CAPEX shock.

anya: +1 staging. ok team — that'll get us into vendor lead-time window if finance moves fast. :thumbsup:

zara: i'll post the draft here when ready. tagging @simon @anya for visibility.

devon: thanks, closing loop — we'll review the doc next Tuesday at 10am PT.
